questions.q: If (1 + cos A)(1 − cos A) = 3/4, find sec A (A acute).
questions.answer:
1 − cos²A = 3/4 ⇒ sin²A = 3/4 ⇒ sin A = √3/2 ⇒ A = 60°.
sec A = sec 60° = 2.

An observer 40 m from a building sees the top and bottom of a flagstaff on the building at elevations of 60° and 45°. Find the height of the building and the length of the flagstaff.
questions.answer:
Building: tan 45° = h/40 ⇒ h = 40 m.
Top of flagstaff: tan 60° = H/40 ⇒ H = 40√3 = 69.28 m.
Flagstaff = 69.28 − 40 = 29.28 m.

questions.q: A tree breaks in a storm; its top touches the ground 2√3 m from the foot, making 60° with the ground. Find the original height.
questions.answer:
Standing part: tan 60° = h₁/2√3 ⇒ h₁ = 2√3 × √3 = 6 m.
Broken part: cos 60° = 2√3/l ⇒ l = 4√3 ≈ 6.93 m.
Height = 6 + 4√3 ≈ 12.93 m.

questions.q: The upper part of a tree broken by the wind makes 30° with the ground, touching it 10 m from the foot. Find the total height of the tree.
A man on top of a 120 m tower sees two cars on opposite sides of the tower, in line with its base, at depressions of 60° and 45°. Find the distance between the cars. (√3 = 1.732)
From the top of a 100 m lighthouse, the angle of depression of a ship changes from 30° to 45° as it sails towards the lighthouse. Find the distance travelled. (√3 = 1.732)
questions.answer:
Let the lighthouse be AB = 100 m, first position C, second D.
At 30°: BC = 100/tan 30° = 100√3 = 173.2 m.
At 45°: BD = 100/tan 45° = 100 m.
Distance CD = 173.2 − 100 = 73.2 m.

or.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of a tower is 30°, and of the top of the tower from the foot of the building is 60°. The tower is 50 m high. Find the height of the building.
or.answer:
Let the distance between them be d.
Tower: tan 60° = 50/d ⇒ d = 50/√3.
Building: tan 30° = h/d ⇒ h = d/√3 = 50/3 ≈ 16.67 m.

questions.q: The shadow of a tower is 10 m longer when the sun's elevation is 30° than when it is 45°. Find the height of the tower. (√3 = 1.732)
questions.answer:
Let the height be h. Shadow at 45° = h; at 30° = h√3.
h√3 − h = 10 ⇒ h = 10/(√3 − 1) = 10/0.732 ≈ 13.66 m.

or.q: An aeroplane 3000 m high passes vertically above another at an instant when their elevations from a point on the ground are 60° and 45°. Find the vertical distance between them.
or.answer:
Horizontal distance d: tan 60° = 3000/d ⇒ d = 3000/√3 = 1000√3 = 1732 m.
Lower plane: height = d tan 45° = 1732 m.
Vertical distance = 3000 − 1732 = 1268 m.

questions.q: From the top of a 100 m tower, two cars on opposite sides are seen at depressions of 60° and 45°. Find the distance between them.

or.q: From a point P on level ground, tan of the elevation of a tower's top is 1/2. After walking 192 m towards the tower, it becomes 3/4. Find the height and the distance of the second point from the tower.
or.answer:
Let the height be h and the second point's distance x.
h/(x + 192) = 1/2 and h/x = 3/4 ⇒ x = 4h/3.
2h = 4h/3 + 192 ⇒ 2h/3 = 192 ⇒ h = 288 m; x = 384 m.

questions.q: A building is 60 m high. From its top the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a tower are 45° and 60°. Find the height of the tower and its distance from the building.
questions.answer:
Distance d = 60/tan 60° = 20√3 ≈ 34.64 m.
Top of tower is d tan 45° = 34.64 m below the building's top.
Tower height = 60 − 34.64 = 25.36 m.

or.q: Two men on either side of an 80 m cliff see its top at elevations of 30° and 60°. Find the distance between them.

questions.q: A person on a river bank sees the top of a tree on the opposite bank at 60°. Moving 40 m back, the angle is 30°. Find the height of the tree and the width of the river.
questions.answer:
Let the width be x and the height h. h = x√3 and h = (x + 40)/√3.
3x = x + 40 ⇒ x = 20 m; h = 20√3 ≈ 34.64 m.

questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of a 150 m tower is 30°, and of the tower's top from the building's foot is 60°. Find the building's height.
questions.answer:
Distance d = 150/tan 60° = 150/√3 = 50√3 m.
Building = d tan 30° = 50√3 × 1/√3 = 50 m.
